title: Folk psychology radically misdescribes the mind, so its posits pick out nothing

statements.text: The central tenets of folk psychology radically misdescribe cognitive processes, so its posits have no role in a serious scientific theory of the mind, because they pick out nothing real. Like dualists, eliminativists hold that ordinary mental states cannot be reduced to neural events, but not because they are nonphysical: because, as commonsense describes them, they do not exist.

sources.quote: the posits of folk psychology have no role to play in a serious scientific theory of the mind because the posits pick out nothing that is real
it is because mental states, as described by common-sense psychology, do not really exist
